blurb: Clovis III is a classical C++17 UCI chess engine by Jonathan McDermid, written as a successor to Hopper Chess. It pairs magic bitboards and a Texel-tuned tapered evaluation with principal variation search, internal iterative deepening, null move pruning, reverse futility pruning, and logarithmic late move reductions. Adapted to UCI over WASI under the deaf profile.
fidelityNotes: Deaf profile (reads input between searches, not mid-search) and single-threaded. Compared with stable-sort.patch on both builds because std::sort orders equal-score moves differently under libstdc++ and libc++.

features.label: Magic Bitboards
features.implementation: 64-bit magic bitboards for sliding-piece attack lookups.

features.label: PVS
features.implementation: Negamax principal variation search with null-window probes and re-searches on fail-high.

features.label: Aspiration Windows
features.implementation: Root aspiration window from depth 3 with progressive widening on fail-high or fail-low.

features.label: Quiescence Search
features.implementation: Horizon capture search with stand-pat cutoffs and transposition table probing.

features.label: Internal Iterative Deepening
features.implementation: Precomputed reduced-depth search when no hash move is available at high depth.

features.label: Null Move Pruning
features.implementation: Reduced-depth null-move pruning enabled from depth 3.

features.label: Reverse Futility Pruning
features.implementation: Static evaluation margin pruning at shallow non-PV nodes.

features.label: Late Move Reductions
features.implementation: Log-log reduction table adjusted by quiet move history scores.

features.label: Countermove & Killers
features.implementation: Killer moves and countermove heuristic beside MVV-LVA and static exchange evaluation.

features.label: Pawn Hash Table
features.implementation: Dedicated hash cache storing evaluated pawn structure scores.

features.label: Tapered Eval
features.implementation: Texel-tuned middlegame and endgame evaluation with PSQTs, mobility, outposts, pawn structure, and king safety.
